newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Late selling hits Belgian bonds, market "feels bad".
newsitem.headline: Late selling hits Belgian bonds, market "feels bad".

text.p: A late spate of selling, particularly in the longer maturities, pushed Belgian linear bonds to a lower close on Wednesday and traders said it was impossible to tell if the move down would continue on Thursday.

"The selling started in the late afternoon. It had been really quiet for the rest of the day. There is a bad feeling in the market and people want to keep their books flat at the end of the day," one trader said.
"It is not a panic movement. Rather it is a quiet decline. It is difficult to tell if it will continue tomorrow," he added.
Traders said the focus was on the longer maturity paper -- 10 years and over -- with little interest in the shorter maturities.
"The curve is steepening again in the longer end," one trader noted.
Traders said domestic and foreign players were active on Wednesday on both sides of the market.
They noted that investors were likely to remain wary ahead of Friday's U.S. employment statistics.
"They will determine the future direction of the market," one trader said.
Traders were mixed over whether the bulk of the more than 60 billion francs in bond coupons paid out last Friday had all been reinvested in the bond markets.
"There was some good buying last week, so I think most has come back," one trader said.
However, others said a fair quantity had moved into the money markets for the time being until calm returned to the bond markets.
The yield of the benchmark 2007 OLO ended at 6.14 percent, up from Tuesday's 6.11. The spread over 10-year German Bunds was at an unchanged 13 basis points.
